tools.name: The Career Layer Excavation Worksheet
tools.content:
# The Career Layer Excavation Worksheet
**Purpose:** Separate the expertise you *own* from the professional identity your employer trained you to perform — so you can name one specific, chargeable consulting offer by the end of this page.

---

## PART 1 — Strip Out the Performed Identity (15 min)

These are things your corporate environment *gave* you that feel like expertise but are actually costume. Cross them off the list you're building in your head.

Answer each prompt in a sentence or two:

**1a.** What was the job title or function you were most publicly associated with?
> *e.g. "Head of Regulatory Affairs," "Senior Brand Manager," "Partner-track employment solicitor"*
> Your answer: [YOUR TITLE / FUNCTION]

**1b.** What did that role require you to *perform* fluently — skills that belong to that institution, not to you?
> *e.g. "Navigating our specific internal approval process," "Managing up to that particular executive team," "Knowing our firm's client base"*
> Your answer: [INSTITUTION-SPECIFIC SKILLS TO SET ASIDE]

**1c.** If you had moved to a competitor on the same day you went on maternity leave, what knowledge would you have carried with you that they would have *immediately* valued?
> Your answer: [PORTABLE KNOWLEDGE — keep this]

---

## PART 2 — Excavate the Real Expertise (20 min)

Work through the three columns below. Fill in every row you can. Leave blanks rather than guess.

| **Role / Project / Period** | **The specific problem I was the person others called about** | **The outcome my involvement produced (concrete, not vague)** |
|---|---|---|
| [e.g. Regulatory affairs lead, 2008–2014] | [e.g. "When a submission was stalled and no one knew why"] | [e.g. "Identified the gap, reframed the dossier section, submission approved in next cycle"] |
| [ROLE / PROJECT / PERIOD] | [SPECIFIC PROBLEM OTHERS BROUGHT TO YOU] | [CONCRETE OUTCOME] |
| [ROLE / PROJECT / PERIOD] | [SPECIFIC PROBLEM OTHERS BROUGHT TO YOU] | [CONCRETE OUTCOME] |
| [ROLE / PROJECT / PERIOD] | [SPECIFIC PROBLEM OTHERS BROUGHT TO YOU] | [CONCRETE OUTCOME] |
| [ROLE / PROJECT / PERIOD] | [SPECIFIC PROBLEM OTHERS BROUGHT TO YOU] | [CONCRETE OUTCOME] |

**Now look at column 2.** Circle the problem type that appears in more than one row — even in different words. That pattern is your expertise. It predates the job title. It will survive the career gap.

---

## PART 3 — Name the Offer (10 min)

Use the pattern you just circled to complete this sentence *exactly as written*:

> **"I help [TYPE OF COMPANY OR PERSON] who are stuck at [SPECIFIC PROBLEM FROM COLUMN 2] get to [CONCRETE OUTCOME FROM COLUMN 3] — without [THE THING THEY DREAD OR HAVE TRIED THAT DIDN'T WORK]."**

Your first draft:
> I help [TYPE OF COMPANY OR PERSON] who are stuck at [SPECIFIC PROBLEM] get to [CONCRETE OUTCOME] — without [THING THEY DREAD].

**Do not edit it for polish yet.** Ugly and specific beats smooth and vague. This sentence is what you say when someone asks what you do — before you have a website, before you have a name for the business, today.

---

**Reality check before you move on:**
- [ ] The problem in my sentence is something a business would *pay* to fix (not just know about)
- [ ] The outcome is a state they can recognise when they've reached it
- [ ] I could have a conversation about this problem for 30 minutes without looking anything up

If all three are checked: you have your niche. Move to Tool 2.
tools.instructions: Work through Parts 1–3 in one sitting (45–60 minutes). Your answer to the final question is your consulting niche — write it on a Post-it and stick it somewhere visible.

tools.name: The First Outreach Message — Swipe Copy (3 Versions)
tools.content:
# The First Outreach Message — Swipe Copy
**Three versions. One for a warm contact you know well, one for a looser professional connection, one for a cold introduction via LinkedIn or email. Fill in brackets. Send.**

---

## VERSION A — Warm Contact (former colleague, friend, peer you've stayed in touch with)

**Subject / opening line:** Catching up — and a question, if you have five minutes

---

Hi [FIRST NAME],

I've been meaning to reach out properly for a while — I hope [PERSONAL DETAIL: e.g. "the new role is going well" / "the renovation survived the winter"] .

I'm in the middle of something new and I'd genuinely value your thinking. After stepping back for [NUMBER] years while the kids were young, I'm returning to work — not back into a salaried role, but consulting in [YOUR NICHE AREA, e.g. "regulatory submissions for mid-size medical device companies"].

I'm not asking you to hire me or refer anyone — I'm just at the stage where talking to people who know that world well would sharpen my thinking. Would you be up for a 20-minute call in the next few weeks?

Either way, would love to hear what you've been up to.

[YOUR NAME]

---

## VERSION B — Looser Professional Connection (former client, conference contact, someone you've emailed a handful of times)

**Subject / opening line:** A quick note — and a question you might enjoy

---

Hi [FIRST NAME],

We worked together / connected at [CONTEXT: e.g. "the CIPD conference in 2017" / "the [COMPANY NAME] project"] — I hope things are going well on your end.

I'm reaching back out because I'm relaunching my professional life after a career pause, and I'm building a consulting practice focused on [SPECIFIC PROBLEM YOU SOLVE, e.g. "helping HR teams restructure onboarding for hybrid workforces without losing the culture work that took years to build"].

Before I go further, I'm speaking with people who are close to that problem — either they've lived it or they commission people to solve it. I'd love 20 minutes of your time to test my thinking, not to pitch anything.

Would that be worth a short call?

[YOUR NAME]
[LINKEDIN PROFILE OR EMAIL SIGNATURE]

---

## VERSION C — Cold Introduction (LinkedIn DM or cold email, no prior relationship)

**Subject / opening line:** A specific question about [THEIR COMPANY NAME / THEIR INDUSTRY]

---

Hi [FIRST NAME],

I came across your profile while researching [THEIR INDUSTRY / ROLE TYPE] and I wanted to reach out directly.

I spent [NUMBER] years in [YOUR FORMER INDUSTRY] working specifically on [SPECIFIC PROBLEM AREA], most recently [BRIEF CREDIBILITY ANCHOR: e.g. "leading submissions across three EU markets for a Series B medical device company"]. After a planned career pause, I'm now returning as an independent consultant.

I'm not pitching anything — I'm at the stage where I'm speaking with [THEIR ROLE TYPE, e.g. "Operations Directors at companies your size"] to understand where [SPECIFIC PROBLEM] tends to be most painful before I finalise how I structure my consulting work.

Would you be open to a 20-minute conversation? I'm happy to work around your schedule.

[YOUR NAME]
[LINKEDIN PROFILE OR RELEVANT LINK]

---

**Sending rules (non-negotiable):**
1. Fill in every bracket before sending — a personalised message with one specific detail outperforms a polished generic one
2. Send 5 this week. Not 2. Not 10. 5.
3. Do not send a follow-up before 5 business days have passed
4. Track replies in Tool 3 — every conversation is data, not just a yes or no
tools.instructions: Pick the version that matches how well you know the recipient, fill in the brackets, and send it before you edit it a third time. Aim for 5 sends this week.

tools.name: The First Paid-Client Conversation — Full Script
tools.content:
# The First Paid-Client Conversation — Full Script
**For use on a 45-minute discovery or 'let's talk further' call with a warm or converted contact. This is the conversation that turns interest into a paying client.**

---

## BEFORE THE CALL — Set Yourself Up (5 min)

- [ ] Your niche sentence from Tool 1 is visible in front of you
- [ ] You know your fee for the first engagement (if unsure: [YOUR DAY RATE] for a paid diagnostic, or [MONTHLY RETAINER] for a 3-month project — pick one before the call)
- [ ] You have a way to take notes (doc, paper — doesn't matter)
- [ ] You are not going to pitch, sell, or convince. Your only job is to understand their problem clearly enough to say whether you can help.

---

## OPENING — First 2 Minutes

**You say:**
> "Thanks so much for making time — I'm glad we're talking properly. I thought the most useful thing I could do is spend the first part of this listening, so I understand your situation before I say anything about my work. Does that sound okay?"

*(They say yes. Good.)*

---

## PHASE 1 — Understand the Problem (15 min)

Ask these questions in order. Don't rush. Let silence do work.

**Question 1:**
> "Tell me about [SPECIFIC PROBLEM AREA from your niche sentence] — what does it look like right now inside your business / team?"

*Listen. Don't fill silence. Note the exact words they use.*

**Question 2:**
> "When this [problem] is at its worst — what's the actual cost? Not just the frustration, but what it's stopping you from doing?"

*Listen. The answer to this question is the value of your work.*

**Question 3:**
> "What have you already tried? And what got in the way?"

*This tells you where your solution needs to be different from what they've already attempted.*

**Question 4:**
> "If this was fully sorted by [TIMEFRAME, e.g. end of Q3] — what would that make possible that isn't possible right now?"

*Note this answer word for word. You'll reflect it back in Phase 3.*

---

## PHASE 2 — Connect Your Expertise (10 min)

**You say:**
> "Can I share what I'm hearing — and then tell you how I've worked on this kind of problem before?"

*(They say yes.)*

> "What I'm hearing is that [MIRROR THEIR WORDS BACK: e.g. 'the submissions process keeps stalling at the same point, and it's holding up your market entry timeline by months']. Is that right?"

*(Let them confirm or correct.)*

> "This is the kind of problem I spent [NUMBER] years working on — specifically [BRIEF SPECIFIC CREDIBILITY STATEMENT: e.g. 'on the dossier and liaison side of EU submissions, where the stall usually happens in one of three identifiable places']. I'm not going to tell you which of those applies to your situation yet — I'd need to look properly — but I recognise what you're describing."

---

## PHASE 3 — Name What You'd Do (10 min)

**You say:**
> "Here's how I'd want to approach this if we worked together."

Then describe your engagement *specifically:*

> "I'd start with [FIRST DELIVERABLE: e.g. 'a two-week diagnostic — I'd review your existing submissions, map where the process is breaking, and give you a written report with three specific changes to make immediately']. From there, [WHAT COMES NEXT: e.g. 'we'd decide together whether you want me to stay involved during the next submission cycle or work from the report independently']."

> "The reason I structure it this way is that it gives you something concrete and usable before you commit to anything larger — and it gives me enough information to be genuinely useful rather than just giving you frameworks."

---

## PHASE 4 — Name the Fee (5 min)

*This is the moment most people lose. The script is short because short is what works.*

**You say:**
> "For the diagnostic I described, my fee is [YOUR FEE]. That includes [WHAT IS INCLUDED: e.g. 'the two-week review, the written report, and a 60-minute debrief call where I walk you through the findings and answer questions']."

**Then stop. Do not fill the silence. Do not discount immediately.**
tools.instructions: Print or pull this up on screen before your first exploratory call. Run the call in this order.

**One page. Updated weekly. Shows you where your three first clients are in the pipeline at any given moment.**

---

**Weekly minimum to hit 3 clients in 90 days:** 5 outreach messages sent / week. Everything else flows from that number.

---

## SECTION 2 — Live Pipeline (your 3 client slots)

Track each active conversation here. One row per person.

| **Contact name** | **How you know them** | **Date of first outreach** | **Current stage** | **Next action** | **Next action by** | **Outcome** |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [NAME] | [e.g. Former colleague] | [DATE] | [e.g. Call booked / Proposal sent / Awaiting reply] | [e.g. Send follow-up email] | [DATE] | [e.g. Client 1 ✓ / Not a fit / Still open] |
| [NAME] | [HOW YOU KNOW THEM] | [DATE] | [STAGE] | [NEXT ACTION] | [DATE] | [OUTCOME] |
| [NAME] | [HOW YOU KNOW THEM] | [DATE] | [STAGE] | [NEXT ACTION] | [DATE] | [OUTCOME] |
| [NAME] | [HOW YOU KNOW THEM] | [DATE] | [STAGE] | [NEXT ACTION] | [DATE] | [OUTCOME] |
| [NAME] | [HOW YOU KNOW THEM] | [DATE] | [STAGE] | [NEXT ACTION] | [DATE] | [OUTCOME] |

---

## SECTION 3 — Friday Check-In (5 questions, 5 minutes)

Answer these every Friday before you close the laptop:

1. **Did I send at least 5 outreach messages this week?** [ ] Yes [ ] No — if no, what got in the way?
2. **Is there anyone in my pipeline I've left waiting more than 5 days without a follow-up?** [ ] Yes → follow up before Monday [ ] No
3. **Did I name my fee in at least one conversation this week?** [ ] Yes [ ] No — if I've had calls but not named a fee, why not?
4. **What's the one thing I heard from a prospect this week that I didn't expect?** [WRITE IT HERE — this is the copy for next week's outreach]
5. **What's my single most important action next Monday morning?** [NAME IT HERE]

---

## SECTION 4 — Stall Diagnostics

If the pipeline has been quiet for two consecutive weeks, work through this:

| **Symptom** | **What it usually means** | **What to do** |
|---|---|---|
| Sending messages but getting no replies | The message is too generic or the ask is too big | Switch to Version A (warm contacts) in Tool 2; reduce the ask to a 20-min call |
| Getting replies but no calls booked | The framing sounds like a pitch, not a conversation | Re-read your message — does it ask for a favour or sell a service? Rewrite toward curiosity |
| Calls going well but no fees named | Avoidance — the call is ending before you reach Phase 4 | Set a timer. Name the fee with 10 minutes left on every call, without exception |
| Fees named but no yeses | Fee too high for first engagement, or problem not felt urgently enough | Offer the diagnostic as a smaller first step; revisit Tool 1 to tighten the problem statement |
| Everything stalled, no momentum | Too much time between actions | Go back to Section 1 — send 5 messages today, not tomorrow |
tools.instructions: Copy this into a spreadsheet or print it. Update it every Friday. The tracker shows you where momentum is — and where to push this week.

promise: Use the four tools in this kit to name your consulting niche out loud, script your first outreach message, and run your first paid-client conversation — starting today, using the professional expertise you already have. No new qualifications, no perfected website, no more notes app.

nextStep.body: The worksheet named your niche. The swipe copy got you into conversations. The script got you through the fee. What the toolkit can't do is run the Career Layer Excavation Process on your actual career — the one that produces a forensic, specific consulting offer traceable back to expertise you already have, not one you constructed to sound credible. That's the work we do live, in one focused session, and you leave holding the first three client conversations scripted at the sentence level.
